text: Both Snowflake views exist. This lesson crosses the real tool boundary: connecting Power BI Desktop to Snowflake, for both teams' data, in one file.

Power BI Desktop ships with a native Snowflake connector. It asks for your account's server hostname, a warehouse — DRIFTWOOD_WH, the same one this chapter's Tasks already use — and, under advanced options, a role: DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST. That role isn't cosmetic. It's the read-only role the Advanced capstone's own RBAC lessons set up specifically for this: analysts and Power BI reading marts, with no ability to touch the pipeline behind them.

After authenticating, Power BI's Navigator shows the marts schema. Check all four views and load them in. Finance's and Support's data ends up in the same file, but as separate tables, each ready to feed its own report page.

Power BI offers Import and DirectQuery. DirectQuery sends a live query to Snowflake on every single visual render. Import pulls a snapshot on a schedule you control. Since this pipeline already refreshes every five minutes through its own Tasks, Import with a modest refresh schedule gives both teams data that's current enough, without hitting the warehouse on every page load.

Before building any visuals, spot-check both imported tables against the baseline numbers from Lesson 8 — catching a mistake now, on flat tables, beats finding it later on a finished page. Next lesson builds Support's actual report page.
